rows.name: Steakhouse Financial
farm_steps: Use a fresh wallet that holds only the funds you plan to farm, and keep its seed phrase offline. Keep at least 0.005 ETH in the wallet: Starknet required at least 0.005 ETH to qualify, and Arbitrum stripped points from wallets under 0.005 ETH that had touched at most one contract. Farm with this one wallet only: LayerZero flagged 803,093 addresses as sybil in 2024. Cost: about $0.01-0.30 of gas for the first transaction on Base. Time: 5 minutes.

Deposit $150 into a Steakhouse Financial vault on Base and check where the curator allocates it and what fee it takes. Then repeat the same deposit once on Ethereum, so the position exists on two chains and the activity is not tied to one of them. Cost: $150 of capital and about $0.01-0.30 of gas per transaction. Gas total (est.): about $0.21-$77 — Base $0.06-$1.8 (6 tx) + Ethereum $0.15-$75 (5 tx). Minimum viable capital (est.): $227 (capital plus gas high end). Time: 15 minutes to set up.

Each week, check the vault's strategy and fee; compound only what the vault itself shows as claimable, and leave the principal in place. Alternate the weekly action between Base and Ethereum, so both chains show activity. Spread the work across at least three distinct months: Arbitrum paid more for activity in 2, 6 and 9 distinct months, and Starknet required at least 3 months. Cost: about $0.01-$0.30 a week on Base, about $0.03-$15 a week on Ethereum in alternate weeks (est.). Time: 10 minutes a week.

Hold the position for at least 60 days so the activity is counted in more than one snapshot window. If the curator changes the allocation or raises the fee, compare the new terms with the first month's before deciding to stay. Leave the deposit in place: zkSync weighted rewards by time-weighted balance, so moving funds in and out counts for less than holding them. Cost: the $150 stays in the position. Time: 60 days.

Check the protocol's own points or rewards page to see whether it runs a programme; if it does, follow only the link that page publishes, and never pay a fee to claim. Points sometimes never convert: in 2026 StandX cancelled its token and Zeta withdrew its migration, so treat points as a hope, not a promise. For a Risk Curators protocol, look first at the rewards section of the protocol's own app. Check once, then again only if the protocol announces a change. Cost: no fee to check, and never pay to claim. Time: 10 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash in a farm log so you can repeat the position or unwind it safely. Log each chain separately, with the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash per chain, so a position on Ethereum can be unwound without touching Base. The whole plan takes about 2h 5m of active time across 60 days: 15 minutes to set up, 9 weekly checks of 10 minutes, 10 minutes to check for a programme, 5 to log. Cost: nothing but the log. Time: 5 minutes.

Keep at least 0.005 ETH in the wallet: Starknet required at least 0.005 ETH to qualify, and Arbitrum stripped points from wallets under 0.005 ETH that had touched at most one contract. Farm with this one wallet only: LayerZero flagged 803,093 addresses as sybil in 2024. Cost: about $0.01-0.30 of gas for the first transaction on Mantle. Time: 5 minutes.

Provide $50 of liquidity to Agni Finance's main pool on Mantle and read the fee and impermanent-loss notes first. After 30 days, add a second deposit of $50 only if the protocol's own page shows the first position is still active. Cost: $50 of capital and about $0.01-0.30 of gas per transaction. Gas total (est.): about $0.11-$3.3 across 11 transactions on Mantle. Minimum viable capital (est.): $54 (capital plus gas high end). Time: 15 minutes to set up.

Each week, check the pool's range and the fees earned; collect the fees once and re-add them to the same pool if the range still holds. Spread the work across at least three distinct months: Arbitrum paid more for activity in 2, 6 and 9 distinct months, and Starknet required at least 3 months. Cost: about $0.01-0.30 of gas a week. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Hold the position for at least 60 days so the activity is counted in more than one snapshot window. If the price leaves the pool's range, withdraw and re-enter at the new range instead of holding a dead position. Leave the deposit in place: zkSync weighted rewards by time-weighted balance, so moving funds in and out counts for less than holding them. Cost: the $50 stays in the position. Time: 60 days.

Check the protocol's own points or rewards page to see whether it runs a programme; if it does, follow only the link that page publishes, and never pay a fee to claim. Points sometimes never convert: in 2026 StandX cancelled its token and Zeta withdrew its migration, so treat points as a hope, not a promise. For a Dexs protocol, look first at the rewards section of the protocol's own app. Check once, then again only if the protocol announces a change. Cost: no fee to check, and never pay to claim. Time: 10 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash in a farm log so you can repeat the position or unwind it safely. Log the pool, the range and the fees collected each week, with every transaction hash. The whole plan takes about 2h 5m of active time across 60 days: 15 minutes to set up, 9 weekly checks of 10 minutes, 10 minutes to check for a programme, 5 to log. Cost: nothing but the log. Time: 5 minutes.
